title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
caption_md: The curve shows $f(x) = \frac{3x^2 + 5}{7x^2 - x}$. The dashed line marks the horizontal asymptote $y = \frac{3}{7}$. Notice how, as $x$ grows large in either direction, $f(x)$ settles closer and closer to $\frac{3}{7}$. The key technique: divide numerator and denominator by $x^2$, and every $\frac{k}{x^n}$ term vanishes, leaving only the ratio of leading coefficients. Trace the curve with your eye toward the far left and far right — the gap between $f(x)$ and the asymptote shrinks toward zero in both directions.
